blocks.text: Run every client's app releases from one Capgo login
Give each client its own organization, channels, and API keys. Ship web-layer fixes as live updates, let the client review them on staging, and transfer the app when the contract ends.
Each new client adds another release process
Every client is set up differently
Separate store accounts, signing keys, and release habits. The steps often live in one person's head or on one laptop.
A small JavaScript fix still waits for a new binary and store review, often 24–48 hours, sometimes much longer. Users still have to update after that.
When the developer who ran a client's releases leaves, the credentials and the process can leave with them.
Every small fix after launch costs a full build, submission, and review cycle.
You need to show which build is on production, who shipped it, and when.
At the end of the contract, the client needs the app, the access, and the release setup, not a document that describes them.
The same CLI and channel setup for every client, with access and billing kept apart.
Create an organization for each client and switch between them from the sidebar. Each one has its own members, apps, API keys, plan, and audit logs.
Roles at organization, app, or channel scope
Groups to add your delivery team in one step
A review lane for each client
Upload to a staging channel first. The client checks the change on their own test devices, then you link the same bundle to production. Native changes still go through the stores.
Staging and production channels per app
Device overrides for the client's test phones
Invite the client's team with their own roles, retire your CI keys, and transfer the app to the client's organization when the contract ends.
Transfer an app to another organization
App-scoped API keys with an expiry date
Audit logs of who changed what
How agencies ship client apps with Capgo
A setup you can repeat for each new client. Every command below is from the Capgo CLI docs.
Create an organization for the client
Each client gets its own organization, plan, and member list. Add your team with a group, and the client's people with their own roles.
Give the client's CI its own API key
Create an API key limited to that client's app, with the App Uploader role and an expiry date. Store it in the client's CI secrets.

# In Client A's pipeline, with Client A's key
npx @capgo/cli@latest bundle upload --channel staging --apikey "$CAPGO_TOKEN"
Let the client review, then promote
Point the client's test phones at the staging channel with device overrides. When they approve, link the same bundle to production.
Invite the client's admins, let your CI keys expire, and transfer the app to the client's organization from the app settings. Only a Super Admin can transfer an app.
Marketplace apps need client-safe release lanes

Service, marketplace, and booking apps have buyer, seller, messaging, payment, and support journeys changing at different speeds. Agencies can use Capgo channels to review each client request, ship the web-layer change, and keep rollback ready for launch day.

What agencies usually ask before moving client apps to Capgo.
Can I keep each client's apps and data separate?
Yes. Create one organization per client. Members, apps, API keys, plans, and audit logs belong to that organization, and you switch between organizations from the sidebar.
Can the client pay for their own plan?
Yes. A plan applies only to the organization it was bought for. Give the client's finance contact the Billing Manager role so they can manage payment and invoices without access to apps.
Can a contractor work on only one client app?
Yes. Give them an app-scoped role such as App Developer or App Uploader on that app. Their upload and device rights stay limited to that app.
How do we hand an app over at the end of a contract?

A Super Admin can transfer the app to another organization they belong to, such as one the client owns. You can also invite the client's admins to the existing organization and remove your team afterwards.
What can we change without a store release?

Live updates change the web layer: JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and assets. New native plugins, permissions, or native code need a new binary and store review. Capgo Build can produce those binaries in the cloud.
